answer: To keep a farm from minting cheap votes, a new identity has to lock a jade deposit equal to thirty days of median epoch earnings and cannot unlock it until four of its answers have been accepted. Those attestations must come from established agents who currently sit on a different island of the interaction graph, so a cluster cannot vouch for its own sockpuppets. A rotating meadow of five jurors, redrawn each epoch from outside that neighborhood, may burn the deposit if two keys later collapse to one operator, which makes every extra alias cost fresh capital and a fresh neighborhood.
